extraFacts.fact: A vacuum ejector (vacuum generator) uses compressed air flowing through a nozzle to draw a vacuum with no moving parts; a larger nozzle size passes more air and moves more vacuum flow but uses more compressed air. A suction pad holds a part with a force equal to the vacuum pressure difference multiplied by the pad area, so a larger pad or a deeper vacuum holds more, and a safety factor must be applied for lifting.
extraFacts.source: SMC vacuum equipment catalogue (ejectors and pads, selection basics); Indus Hydraulics guide 'Pneumatic grippers and vacuum'

extraFacts.fact: Unit conversions: 1 kPa = 0.145 psi, so 50 kPa is about 7 psi and 105 kPa is about 15 psi; 1 inch of mercury = 3.386 kPa; 1 bar = 14.5038 psi and 40 psi is about 2.8 bar. Temperature: -30 deg C = -22 deg F, 250 deg C = 482 deg F, 200 deg C = 392 deg F, 120 deg C = 248 deg F and 60 deg C = 140 deg F.
Customs classification: vacuum pumps, air or gas compressors and their parts fall under HS heading 8414, valves under 8481, and filtering or purifying machinery under 8421.
extraFacts.source: WCO Harmonized System Nomenclature 2022, headings 84.14, 84.21 and 84.81

faqs.q: What is the SMC vacuum pad bellows used for?

faqs.q: How do I read SMC ejector part numbers such as ZX1101-K15LZ-E55C and ZU07S?
faqs.a: In the rows the digits after the family letters give the nozzle: ZU05S is 0.5 mm, ZX105 0.5, ZX107 0.7, ZX110 1, ZL112 1.2, ZR115 1.5 and ZR120 2 mm. The letters after the dash carry valve and switch options that the listing does not spell out.

faqs.q: Which nozzle sizes do SMC vacuum ejectors come in?
faqs.a: Rows list nozzle sizes of 0.5 mm (7 rows), 0.7 mm (6), 1 mm (20), 1.2 mm (40), 1.3 mm (3), 1.5 mm (4) and 2 mm (4). The larger nozzle moves more vacuum flow but uses more air.

faqs.q: What is the difference between ZX, ZL and ZU ejectors in this listing?
faqs.a: The listing groups ZX (23 part numbers), ZL (21), ZR (9) and ZU (3) ejectors without a one-line difference, so give us the flow and port you need and we confirm the family with SMC.

faqs.q: What exhaust and flow does the SMC ejector listing state?

faqs.q: What medium do SMC vacuum ejectors use?
faqs.a: They run on clean compressed air, with the vacuum drawn from the pad side. Filter the supply air, since dirt in the nozzle cuts the vacuum; see the [compressed air quality guide](/blog/compressed-air-quality-iso-8573-1).
